items.finding: Low-level fusion concatenates FTIR and Raman spectra before training a separate PLSR model, with SNV applied to both spectral blocks before concatenation.
items.how_it_applies: This could inform testing a low-level fusion workflow for Raman and MIR-ATR, where each block is preprocessed and concatenated before model training.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The study used liposome samples and laboratory FTIR/Raman instruments, not cell-culture medium or in-line same-spot sampling.

citation.quote: The low-level fusion concatenates the dataset for the FTIR and Raman spectra (see Figure 4) prior to training a separate PLSR model, and this was achieved by applying the SNV to both the FTIR and Raman spectra prior to concatenation.
citation.label: E04 ¶37

items.finding: In one study, models based on the infrared modality alone performed best for detecting fish oil adulteration, suggesting fusion does not always improve over a single method.
items.how_it_applies: This supports the requirement to compare a fused model against the best single method on held-out runs before keeping the extra instrument.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The study concerned marine oils and laboratory spectroscopy, not cell-culture glucose/lactate or in-line Raman/MIR-ATR.

citation.quote: However, they also found that the models based on the infrared modality alone performed the best for detecting generic fish oil adulteration in cod liver and salmon oils, indicating that there are other strategies available to achieve better precision and accuracy with machine learning models.
citation.label: E04 ¶11

items.finding: Raman is frequently used in upstream processing because of high selectivity and low water interference, though measurement times are relatively long.
items.how_it_applies: For O2, this suggests Raman may handle aqueous medium but response time should be tested against the process need.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source does not give glucose- or lactate-specific detection limits or accuracy, and upstream processing may differ from this cell-culture medium and in-line setup.

citation.quote: Raman spectroscopy is frequently applied in upstream processing in research and industry due to its high selectivity and low water interference [55] despite the relatively long measurement times.
citation.label: E02 ¶20
